history.summary: Despite an 848 score, this is not cheap — it's priced at the top of the project's current $1,578-$1,667 psf range and carries a +8.9% cohort premium. A 431sqft Geylang shoebox with financing/liquidity baggage and a thin-data appreciation story.
history.rating_rationale: The high score is misleading here. Asking $1,578 psf sits at the very bottom-but-still-inside the current project band of $1,578-$1,667 psf, and crucially psf_premium_vs_cohort is +8.9% — a PREMIUM to its own size cohort, not a discount. The eye-catching 11.6% appreciation_pct rests on just 15 transactions, which under the v3.4 priors I treat as noise, not forward signal. The age_adj_premium -18.5% conflicts with the positive cohort premium and the at-market web pricing, so the 'cheap' read is unreliable. Substantively this is a 431sqft shoebox in Geylang on Lorong 6 — closer to the red-light belt than the safer even-Lorong 24-38 stretch — where banks restrict or refuse financing in parts, materially hurting resale liquidity. Shoebox + Geylang stigma + at/above-market entry + thin data is a poor combination for a 5-7yr investment hold. The only real positives (freehold, D14 yield) don't offset paying a premium for an illiquid asset.
red_flags: Not cheap: psf_premium_vs_cohort +8.9% — a premium to its own size cohort; asking is at the top of the live $1,578-$1,667 band
11.6% CAGR built on only 15 txns — likely data quirk, not durable trend (v3.4: trailing appreciation ~0 forward power)
431sqft shoebox — narrow buyer pool, MAS shoebox sensitivity, weaker financing
Lorong 6 Geylang — near red-light belt; documented bank-financing restrictions and harder resale liquidity
Conflicting signals (age_adj -18.5% vs cohort +8.9%) undermine the cheapness thesis
catalysts: Freehold tenure (no lease decay) — but not a forward return edge under v3.4
D14 strong rental yields (3.5-4.5%) for income-only holds
Very long-run en-bloc optionality if the Geylang red-light designation recedes — speculative

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: A 431sqft FH shoebox in Geylang can rent well on yield given the low absolute price, but tenant quality/turnover and the area stigma weigh on it; income is the only real merit and doesn't justify a premium entry.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: I assign no weight to the 11.6% trailing CAGR (15 txns). Paying a cohort premium for a shoebox in a financing-constrained, stigmatized micro-location points to below-market forward capital growth and a difficult exit.
